figures.label: fig:coevox-teaser
figures.caption: Brain--body alignment in model--harness co-evolution. Left: Historical harnesses and checkpoints are recombined and adapted to resolve interface mismatch. Right: Step accuracy versus Turn-level Interface Mismatch Rate (TIMR; sec:coevolution) for ten evolved versions per method, from a three-round run evaluated on the Who\&When test benchmark.

figures.label: fig:whowhen-harness-evolution
figures.caption: Co-evolution on Who\&When Algo. Dashed/solid curves show AA/SA, and marker labels give TIMR (\%). Panels show harnesses at rounds 6--8. The left panel compares full with Harness-only, Model-only, and Latest-only evolution across ten rounds. The right panels connect selected rounds to actor-summary recovery, budget-aware evidence coverage, and evidence rechecking, including reuse of round-4 model weights. Full improves accuracy while keeping TIMR at or below 0.22\%, illustrating the complementary roles of joint adaptation and historical inheritance.

figures.label: fig:rbac-harness-evolution
figures.caption: Harness evolution on role-aware text-to-SQL. Safe-EX and violation rate over ten rounds, with designs from rounds 3, 4, and 9. Blue circles and purple squares track Safe-EX and violation rate on the left and right axes, respectively. Dashed connectors link the selected rounds to evidence-backed refusal, authorization of all SQL references, and verification with bounded repair. Across the run, Safe-EX rises from 77.09\% to 80.85\%, while violation rate falls from 2.00\% to 1.57\%, a 21.5\% relative reduction.

figures.label: fig:pareto-cost
figures.caption: Inference cost--accuracy trade-offs. uses OpenRouter's Qwen3.5-9B pricing. The left and right panels report Who accuracy on Who\&When Hand and Safe-EX on RBAC Spider against the cost of a full evaluation pass, using a logarithmic cost axis. Dashed staircases and shaded regions summarize the baseline Pareto frontiers, while stars mark the co-evolved 9B agent.

figures.label: fig:lineage-heatmap
figures.caption: Interface compatibility on RBAC. Normalized TIMR ( ) across harness--checkpoint pairs; only the lower triangle is available during evolution. Rows index evolved harnesses and columns index model checkpoints, with TIMR globally min--max scaled to [0,1] across the complete matrix for comparison. Stars identify selected pairs and aliased checkpoints, and the side and bottom links record derivation, reuse, and historical design references. Low-TIMR off-diagonal pairings and checkpoint reuse show that interface compatibility depends on the particular harness--model pair, motivating inheritance beyond the latest generation.
